title: Little cells with labels
kid: On this big American backbone your parcel is chopped into tiny pieces, all the same size, each with a little label in front. Machines in the middle read only the label, swap it for a new one and send the piece on. At the far end the pieces are glued back into your parcel.
nerd: ATM: fixed 53-byte cells, a 5-byte header and 48 bytes of payload. The router segments each IP packet with AAL5 (RFC 1483 LLC/SNAP, then an 8-byte trailer with length and CRC-32, padded to 48). Switches forward on the VPI/VCI of a permanent virtual circuit and rewrite it hop by hop, much as MPLS would swap labels from 2001. The far router reassembles at the cell marked last (PTI).

describe.kid: Two backbone routers with a line between them, and a switch in the middle. Small square pieces stream along the line, each with an orange label that turns teal as the switch swaps it. One card shows your parcel cut into 32 pieces; the other shows one piece: a small label and a big part of your parcel.
describe.nerd: Two routers joined by an ATM circuit through a switch that rewrites VPI/VCI 1/112 to 1/87. One card shows a 1500-byte packet cut by AAL5 into 32 cells, 1696 bytes on the line; the other a 53-byte cell: VPI/VCI, PTI and CLP, HEC, and 48 bytes of payload.
